Fundación BBVA: benefactor for four years under an agreement signed 2 January 2025, 625,000 euros a year and 2,500,000 euros in total, supporting the Grandes Exposiciones programme and audiovisual projects (state gazette BOE, 14 January 2025).
Benefactors Fundación BBVA (2025) and Fundación AXA (2024).
Multi-year grants also came from Fundación La Caixa (2018 to 2028) and the BBVA foundation (2020 to 2023).

Glassell family, Lynn and Oscar Wyatt, the Brown Foundation, the Sarah Campbell Blaffer Foundation, the Duncan Foundation, the Cullen Foundation and the Wortham Foundation; the largest corporate gift was $5 million from BBVA Compass Bank (CultureMap Houston, 16 January 2015).
Corporate Supporters include Iberdrola Scottish Power, BBVA and Rothschild & Co.
Founded in 2011 by the bank Garanti BBVA; a member of L'Internationale since 2013 and of the International Confederation of Architectural Museums since 2024.
Garanti BBVA founded Salt in 2011; Hyperallergic calls Garanti "one of the biggest financial institutions in Turkey" and Salt's primary funder.

Salt general manager Deniz Ova thanked the founder Garanti BBVA for its support, and Garanti BBVA deputy general manager Ebru Taşcı Firuzbay is a Salt board member (Garanti BBVA release, 22 May 2026; translated from Turkish).
Wikipedia states that Garanti BBVA owns Salt's three exhibition spaces, including the Ankara space.
Salt Research Funds, a grants programme since 2013, has supported more than 80 projects; in 2025 the Garanti BBVA Economic History Fund expanded it (Garanti BBVA release).
Founded by Garanti BBVA in 2011.

Garanti BBVA brought together Platform Garanti Contemporary Art Center, the Ottoman Bank Archives and Research Centre and Garanti Gallery, whose resources were transferred to Salt (Salt, History page).
Garanti BBVA's release of 22 May 2026 says Salt has had about 5 million visitors and has opened over 2 million archive documents and sources to public access (translated from Turkish).
Founded and funded by Garanti BBVA (bank) since 2011.
Parent Garanti BBVA posts reports 2000 to 2025, accounts and a board list.
The Fukutake Foundation and Benesse Corporation run Benesse Art Site Naoshima, whose museums span Naoshima, Teshima and Inujima; it takes part in the Setouchi Triennale.
The activities are conducted by Benesse Corporation and the Fukutake Foundation (Benesse Art Site).
Fukutake describes a concept he calls "public interest capitalism": corporations set up foundations that become major shareholders, and the dividends fund the foundations' work (Benesse Art Site).
Benesse Corporation, an education and publishing company in Okayama, was founded in 1955 as Fukutake Publishing by Tetsuhiko Fukutake.
Soichiro Fukutake succeeded his father as president in 1986 (Wikipedia, Benesse).
On 10 November 2023 BPEA EQT, an EQT fund, announced a tender offer to take Benesse Holdings private in partnership with the founding family; Benesse's board recommended it (EQT press release).

The Fukutake Education and Culture Foundation in Okayama (fukutake.or.jp) funds education and culture grants and lists the art site among linked organisations; its pages show no funding of the museums.

The collective name for all art activities run by Benesse Corporation and the Fukutake Foundation on Naoshima and Teshima in Kagawa Prefecture and Inujima in Okayama Prefecture (stated by Benesse Art Site).

Benesse Corporation began on Naoshima in 1989 with a campsite, opened Benesse House, a hotel and art museum complex, in 1992, started the Art House Project in the Honmura district in 1998, and opened the Chichu Art Museum in 2004 (Mecenat, a Japanese corporate philanthropy association).

Soichiro Fukutake, Honorary Chairman of the Fukutake Foundation and General Producer of the Setouchi Triennale, began visiting Naoshima to continue his father's project of building a children's campsite there (stated by Benesse Art Site).
Buildings: the Chichu Art Museum and Benesse House were designed by Tadao Ando (Wikipedia, Naoshima).

Museums listed on the site: Naoshima New Museum of Art, Chichu, Benesse House Museum, Teshima Art Museum and Inujima Seirensho Art Museum, plus the Lee Ufan Museum, the Art House Project and the Hiroshi Sugimoto Gallery.
In July 2014 Benesse Corporation announced a leak of customer personal data, with a maximum of about 20.7 million records; police began an investigation on 7 July (Gigazine, 9 July 2014).
Benesse Corporation funds the art site; the leak concerns the company, not the museums.
Built by the Benesse Foundation, funded by Benesse Corporation (Fukutake family).
EFU Investments and a BPEA EQT fund bought 70.1% of Benesse in March 2024.
The Fukutake Foundation, which runs the art, lists yearly plans and reports from FY2007 and a dated board.
Cultural revitalization initiative across Naoshima, Teshima, and Inujima founded by Soichiro Fukutake.
Fukutake Foundation: with Benesse it conducts the activities grouped as Benesse Art Site Naoshima (Benesse Art Site Naoshima website).
The project is funded by the foundation, which runs on dividends from its shares in Benesse Holdings (The Peak, 22 December 2016).

Benesse Holdings: the education and publishing company behind the art site, and the source of the Fukutake fortune; The Peak put Soichiro Fukutake's fortune at an estimated US$1.1 billion in 2016 and described Benesse as the company behind the Berlitz language schools.
Operator named in a corporate patronage listing: the museum is 'operated by Naoshima Fukutake Art Museum Foundation' (Association for Corporate Support of the Arts, Japan, mecenat.or.jp).

Board: Hideaki Fukutake has chaired the Fukutake Foundation since January 2023, chairs the board of Benesse Holdings and founded efu Investment Ltd. in New Zealand; Soichiro Fukutake is honorary chairman of the foundation and honorary advisor of Benesse Holdings (Fukutake Foundation press release, 22 October 2024).

It opened in July 2004 as part of Benesse Art Site Naoshima, whose origins the site traces to Tetsuhiko Fukutake, founding president of Fukutake Publishing, and Chikatsugu Miyake, then mayor of Naoshima (Benesse Art Site Naoshima history page).
Soichiro Fukutake chose three artists so that each work has room (The Peak, 22 December 2016).
Part of Benesse Art Site Naoshima, the collective name for the art activities of Benesse and the Fukutake Foundation (Benesse Art Site Naoshima website).
The Peak reported on 22 December 2016 that the project is funded by Soichiro Fukutake's foundation, which runs on dividends from its shares in Benesse Holdings.
The pages read did not show any published accounts for the museum or the Fukutake Foundation.
A museum built underground on Naoshima, designed by Tadao Ando and opened in July 2004, holding works by Claude Monet, James Turrell and Walter De Maria (Benesse Art Site Naoshima website).

The Fukutake Foundation is chaired by Hideaki Fukutake, who also chairs the board of Benesse Holdings, with Soichiro Fukutake as honorary chairman (Fukutake Foundation press release, 22 October 2024).
The mayor of Tokamachi chairs the committee and the general producer is Soichiro Fukutake (honorary adviser of Benesse Holdings and honorary chairman of the Fukutake Foundation).
Its about page names Reiko Fukutake as founder.
The Setouchi Triennale executive committee includes the chairman and honorary chairman of the Fukutake Foundation.
English Wikipedia lists the support as a combination of funds from the Fukutake Foundation, the Fukutake family's own investments, Benesse and government backing.

English Wikipedia describes it as launched as a public-private partnership between the local prefectural and municipal governments and Benesse, an education publisher, and calls the Benesse Art Site the collective title for the Benesse-initiated art projects on Naoshima, Teshima and Inujima.
Japanese Wikipedia lists Soichiro Fukutake as general producer.
The festival's page lists him as Honorary Adviser (Honorary Chairman, Fukutake Foundation).
Hideaki Fukutake is chairman of the Fukutake Foundation (Setouchi Triennale).
Executive committee led by Kagawa Prefecture and the Fukutake Foundation.
In May 2021 Netflix and Amazon Studios paused work with it, WarnerMedia later joined them, and on 10 May 2021 NBC said it would not air the 2022 Golden Globes.
Institutional partners on the corporate-support page archived 26 May 2026 include Amazon, Alaska Airlines and Bloomberg Philanthropies.

Griffin, the Northrop Grumman Foundation, Textron, American Airlines, Airbus, BAE Systems, Lockheed Martin and Amazon, among 118 entries (museum website; no amounts or years).
Corporate subscribers 2025-2026 include Amazon Ads, Assolombarda, Banca Aletti - Banco BPM, Banca Sella, Deloitte Italy, J.T.

The founding working group was Ajay Desai, Anita Dube, Bharti Kher, Subodh Gupta, Prithpal Singh Ladi, Manisha Parekh and Pooja Sood, and Sood is currently its director (Wikipedia).

Advisory board: Richard Armstrong (chairman), Princess Alia Al-Senussi, Bharti Kher, Chittrovanu Mazumdar, Shaikha Maisa Al Qassimi, Maya Allison, Sandhini Poddar, Smita Prabhakar, Sasha Altaf and Sabih Ahmed.
USA Art News also names building donors Kiran Mazumdar Shaw, Sunil Munjal, Citi and Tata.
Building donors include Kiran Mazumdar Shaw, Sunil Munjal, Citi and Tata.

The Holburne Museum's supporter page lists the Blavatnik Family Foundation but does not specify the timing, amount, share or terms of its support.
Bellingcat's 2019 profile concerns Blavatnik and the Council on Foreign Relations; it does not report on Holburne or establish the museum's funding relationship.

Trusts and foundations listed on the supporters page include AKO Foundation, Art Fund, the Blavatnik Family Foundation, the Clore Duffield Foundation, the Garfield Weston Foundation, the Henry Moore Foundation, the Linbury Trust, the Wolfson Foundation and the Headley Trust (holburne.org supporters page).
Trusts include Garfield Weston, AKO, Clore Duffield and the Blavatnik Family Foundation; Bloomberg Philanthropies backed the website.

In February 2014 the museum set up an endowment and raised $4.5 million in one evening at a gala dinner; co-founders of the fund were Viktor Vekselberg, Leonard Blavatnik, Roman Abramovich, Vadim Moshkovich, Alexey Likhtenfeld, Alexander Klyachin, Gennady Timchenko and Mikhail Gutseriev (Kommersant, Tatyana Markina, 6 February 2014).
Founding donors in 2012 to 2014 included Vekselberg, Abramovich and Blavatnik.

text: The Leonard Blavatnik Foundation stopped supporting projects in Russia after the war began (RTVI).
Major gifts: the Blavatnik Family Foundation gave 10 million pounds in 2022, Randy Lerner 5 million in 2008, and the Heritage Lottery Fund 9.4 million in 2017 toward the refurbishment (Wikipedia).
Blavatnik Family Foundation is listed in 2020 and 2021 and no later.

Wikipedia says Len Blavatnik made his initial fortune in the privatisation of Soviet-era aluminium and oil assets, including an AAR purchase of 40 percent of Tyumen Oil, and that his business controls 21 percent of LyondellBasell.
Blavatnik Family Foundation gave in 2020 and 2021, Bloomberg Philanthropies in 2018 and 2019.
Bloomberg (2018-19) and Blavatnik Family Foundation (2020-21) were partners; neither is listed since, so neither is a current funder.

The Bukhman Foundation supported Alvaro Barrington's Tate Britain Commission and the Art Now 30th anniversary programme; The Julia and Hans Rausing Trust and the Christian Levett Collection supported Now You See Us; the Blavatnik Family Foundation and the Terra Foundation for American Art gave grants to Sargent and Fashion (Tate Annual Report 2024-25).
Supporters: Burberry, The Bukhman Foundation, Gucci, Hyundai Motor, The Julia and Hans Rausing Trust, Blavatnik Family Foundation.

NYC DCLA and NYSCA; Warhol, Frankenthaler, Speyer, Niarchos, Luce and Blavatnik Family foundations, as listed on its 2025 support page.

Bloomberg Philanthropies is a programme supporter and title sponsor of New Contemporaries, which Camden hosted in 2024.
Arts Council England, DCMS, Bloomberg Philanthropies (programme support), trusts including AKO, Foyle, Freelands and Henry Moore, and patrons including Batia and Idan Ofer.
Bloomberg Philanthropies title-sponsored New Contemporaries, shown at Camden in 2024.
PDVSA runs the centre as the social and cultural arm of the oil industry (Bloomberg, Correo Cultural).

In its boom years it paid for urban renewal in central Caracas (Bloomberg); ReVista credits the centre with restoring Jesús Soto's "Orange Sphere", Alejandro Otero's "Abra Solar", Sabana Grande Boulevard and the Torres del Silencio (2008).
PDVSA's social development spending fell 89 percent to 977 million US dollars in its last published annual figures, for 2016 (Bloomberg, 2019).
In 2019 the centre was run by Mary Quevedo, wife of the oil minister; the post traditionally goes to the spouse of PDVSA's president (Bloomberg).
The Caracas site is an 18th-century coffee plantation (Bloomberg) with a garden of more than 120 plant species (Wikipedia, Spanish).
Bloomberg Connects hosts its free guide.
Bloomberg Connects is a free app.

Partners and funders listed: the Belgian federal government, the National Lottery, BNP Paribas Fortis, Proximus, Denys and NextGenerationEU.
Wikipedia lists Bayer, Novartis and UBS as major partners, plus Basler Kantonalbank, BNP Paribas Foundation, Rolls-Royce Motor Cars, ISS Facility Services, J.
Partners: Pictet, BNP Paribas Fortis, De Bethune, Duvel.

Companies and institutions in that circle: Scil Bénin Peinture, Masathis, Ancelle et Associés, La Mode en Images, Fondation H, AKAT, BNP Paribas and Institut Français Paris with the Agence Française de Développement.
Its undated patrons page lists BNP Paribas, Masathis, Institut Français de Paris, Agence Française de Développement and Open Society Foundations.

The Partners Committee's Circle, which names a board member, is Christian Levett, Salvatore Ferragamo, Rocco Forte Hotels, Deloitte, Findomestic (BNP Paribas group), Amanda Platek, Toscana Aeroporti, Gruppo Beyfin, Gucci, Maria Manetti Shrem and Palazzo Strozzi Foundation USA (2025 annual report).

Soho House and BNP Paribas are named in the petition below; the petition says BNP Paribas is still listed as a sponsor of The Freud Circle although the partnership ended in 2019 (petition, not independently checked).
Live petition to drop Hennessy, Soho House and BNP Paribas.

Foundations listed without detail: Art Mentor Foundation Lucerne, Beisheim Stiftung, BNP Paribas Stiftung, Commerzbank-Stiftung, PwC-Stiftung, Sparkassen-Kulturstiftung Rheinland, Ernst von Siemens Kunststiftung, Japan Foundation, Kulturstiftung des Bundes, Kulturstiftung der Länder, Kunststiftung NRW, Rudolf-August Oetker Stiftung, Volkswagenstiftung and others (partners page).
Gifts: Sonatrach handed over 174 canvases by Juanita Guccione in 2012, and BNP Paribas gave two Étienne Dinet paintings in 2012 (French Wikipedia).

Corporate names on the 2025 to 2026 donor list include Citadel, Morgan Stanley, BNP Paribas, Bulgari, Givenchy, Tory Burch, Walgreens, Gagosian and Phillips (each $20,000 to $49,999), Raymond James ($50,000 to $99,999), Sotheby's ($10,000 to $19,999), J.P.
City of Miami Beach ($20M+), Knight Foundation, Miami-Dade Cultural Affairs, Art Bridges, State of Florida. 2025-26 corporate donors at $20,000+: Citadel, Morgan Stanley, BNP Paribas, Walgreens.
BNP Paribas (2025-26 donor) pleaded guilty in 2014 over sanctions and agreed to pay $8.9B.

Student protesters at the University of Melbourne in May 2024 demanded disclosure and divestment of the university's ties to weapons makers, naming Lockheed Martin, Boeing and BAE Systems; on 22 May the university committed to disclose its research grant arrangements (The Melburnian, Georgie Atkins, 28 May 2024).

Wikipedia's funding section on the 2008 New York Philharmonic visit names a donation from Yoko Nagae Ceschina and an Asiana Airlines Boeing 747 provided by the Kumho Asiana Group's chairman, Park Sam Koo.

Green Left (Jacob Andrewartha, "Student encampment forces Uni of Melbourne to disclose weapons ties", 23 May 2024) reported that after a four-week Gaza solidarity encampment and a week-long occupation the University of Melbourne agreed to disclose its funding arrangements with weapons corporations, that Unimelb for Palestine expected disclosure of ties to all weapons manufacturers including Lockheed Martin, Boeing and BAE Systems, and that the university rejected the demand to divest.
A SponsorPitch listing, a snapshot dated 6 November 2014, is headed "Boeing signs on as sponsor for Seattle Art Museum"; it names no exhibition, term or amount.
Boeing and Honeywell, both US defence contractors, are named as institutional partners on the museum's corporate-support page.
Bellingcat matched 79 Gaza strikes to US-made Hellfire missiles, GBU-39 bombs and JDAM kits, naming Lockheed Martin and Boeing as the contractors.
Boeing's 2014 gift names the Milestones of Flight Hall at Air and Space; Lockheed Martin names its IMAX theater.
Building-transformation donors named on the museum's page include Jeff Bezos, Boeing, RTX, the Thomas W.
Boeing's $30 million gift of 2014 for the Boeing Milestones of Flight Hall is described under Red flags.
Boeing, Northrop Grumman and Lockheed name galleries; Koch hall kept.

Founder Boris Mints: The Art Newspaper (Sophia Kishkovsky, 28 June 2018) reported that news of his family's departure for London emerged at the end of May 2018, and that it was unclear whether he would keep funding the museum from the UK; director Petrova declined to discuss his ongoing support.
Unverified: the article cites reports that Mints left to avoid possible criminal investigation in Russia over bank dealings; it names no bank, and O1 Group referred questions to the museum.
Mints has lived in London for several years.

Petrova said he cannot support the museum for legal reasons; Mints said being outside the country prevents him from supporting it adequately, and he still takes part in discussing its development programme and exhibition plans (The Art Newspaper Russia, 15 February 2024).

OpenSanctions lists Mints as a close associate of a politically exposed person (from Wikidata) and as an oligarch (from the Russian Oligarch/Billionaires Database, which mentions a 2018 CAATSA report on Russian oligarchs).
Founded by the collector Boris Mints (O1 Group).
Private: founded by Boris Mints (O1 Group) in 2016; since Feb 2024 the patron-trustee is Vladimir Voronin, shareholder of property developer FSK Group.
Mints left Russia.
No sanctions listing for Mints on OpenSanctions.
An initiative of the Borusan Kocabıyık Foundation.
Borusan Holding decided to institutionalise its visual arts activities through Borusan Contemporary (Borusan Kocabıyık Foundation history page).
The museum sits in the holding's head office; Borusan Holding leased the building in 2002 (Wikipedia).
Borusan Holding is a Turkish industrial group founded in 1944 by Asım Kocabıyık as İstikbal Ticaret; Ahmet Kocabıyık has chaired it since 2001.
Energy: Borusan EnBW Enerji, owned jointly by Borusan Holding and Germany's EnBW AG, has 725 MW of installed capacity in 12 renewable power plants.
Contemporary art, collection and education initiative of the Borusan Kocabıyık Foundation, in the Perili Köşk ("Haunted Mansion"), Baltalimanı Hisar Cad.
The building is also the head office of Borusan Holding.
It is open to the public on weekends (Borusan Kocabıyık Foundation).
Borusan Contemporary opened in September 2011 (Wikipedia).
The Borusan Kocabıyık Foundation says it began operating in 2011 as an economic enterprise of the foundation.
Architect Hakan Kıran led a restoration from 1995 to about 2000, and Borusan Holding began leasing it in 2002 and moved in during 2007 (Wikipedia).
The foundation was set up in 1992 by Asım Kocabıyık and his family and renamed Borusan Kocabıyık Foundation in 2007 (Borusan Kocabıyık Foundation).

Programme: the Borusan Contemporary Art Collection, focused on media art, temporary exhibitions (Olivo Barbieri's "Time Space Geometry" and the collection show "Haunted", 19 September 2026 to 15 August 2027), education programmes, a café and a bookstore.
Corporate museum of Borusan Holding, run by the Borusan Kocabıyık Foundation in the holding's headquarters.
Borusan EnBW Enerji runs 725 MW of renewable plants.
2025 corporate partners: Ploom (main partner), Banca Transilvania (strategic partner), Catena (exhibition partner); supporters ISHO, Bosch, Mewi, Sanmarco and Saint-Gobain (Canvas).
The organisation's history page lists seven founding signatories: Monika Baker, Merle Van Den Bosch, Armet Francis, Sunil Gupta, Michael Jess, George Shire and Lance Watson.

What is there: Venetian and Veneto painting of the 14th to the 18th century in 37 rooms, with works by Giovanni Bellini, Carpaccio, Giorgione, Titian, Veronese, Tintoretto and Giambattista Tiepolo; named works are Giorgione's Tempest, Titian's Pietà, Carpaccio's Legend of Saint Ursula, Veronese's Feast in the House of Levi, Bosch's Hermit Saints Triptych, Paolo Veneziano's Coronation of the Virgin polyptych and Leonardo's Vitruvian Man (museum website).

Programme sponsors: Paribu (free Thursdays), Volvo, İGA Art, Panço, Nescafe, Bosch Ev Aletleri and Visa; Mercedes-Benz sponsors membership; TAV Airports is travel sponsor and Tepta Aydınlatma gives special support (sponsor panel).

Foundations on the same list include Kulturstiftung des Bundes, Stiftung Niedersachsen, Robert Bosch Stiftung, Alfried Krupp von Bohlen und Halbach Stiftung, Braunschweigische Sparkassenstiftung, Die Braunschweigische Stiftung, Stiftung Kunstfonds, Hypo-Kulturstiftung, DZ BANK Kunststiftung and Volkswagen art foundation.

What is there: 158,294 objects were registered at the end of 2025, of which 139,587 are municipal property, and 131,467 of the total are artworks (annual report 2025); the museum says 1,700 private collectors have given 50,000 objects since 1849; the holdings run from old masters (Van Eyck, Bosch, Bruegel, Rembrandt, Rubens, Titian) through Impressionism and a Surrealist collection (Dalí, Magritte, Ernst) to design and contemporary art, with Bruegel's The Tower of Babel and The Three Marys at the Tomb by Jan and/or Hubert van Eyck among the named works; in 2025 it took in 432 objects as gifts, 89 by bequest and 295 by purchase (museum website; annual report 2025).

Individual donors named with a purpose: Leendert Bosch (bequest for restoring the earth and nail collection), Aty van der Drift (inheritance for restoring and expanding the building), Carla van Steijn (gifts and legacies for the building and the collection), Gail and Ernst von Metzsch (restoring the University Room).

What is there: the institutional chambers of the Great Council, the Senate, the Collegio and the Council of Ten; the Museo dell'Opera in six rooms with the capitals removed in the restoration begun in 1876; the Giants' Staircase with Sansovino's Mars and Neptune of 1565; a picture gallery with works by Giovanni Bellini, Carpaccio, Titian, Giambattista Tiepolo and a follower of Bosch; the New Prisons reached by the Bridge of Sighs; and an armoury of over 2,000 exhibits whose core is documented in the 14th century (museum website).

Supporters named on its website: Creative Europe Programme, Allianz Kulturstiftung, Robert Bosch Foundation, Pro Helvetia, European Cultural Foundation, Goethe-Zentrum Tirana, Swiss Cultural Fund Albania, the Italian Ministry of Cultural Heritage and Tourism, the Albanian Ministry of Culture and the Municipality of Tirana, plus several embassies.
Named supporters: Creative Europe, Allianz Kulturstiftung, Pro Helvetia, Robert Bosch Foundation, European Cultural Foundation, Albania's Ministry of Culture, Municipality of Tirana.

Other patrons listed: Dance Reflections by Van Cleef & Arpels, Jacquet Metals, Paprec, SLCI, Artprice by Artmarket, Bouygues Bâtiment Sud-Est, Maison Ruinart, MGEN, Duvel Moortgat France, Banque de France (Biennale website).
Cercle Louvre-Lens members listed include Bouygues Bâtiment Nord-Est, Nexans, NetEase, Enedis, Groupe La Poste, Banque des Territoires and RC Lens (museum patronage site).
Designed by Studio KO and built by the Moroccan subsidiary of Bouygues.
The 2025 accounts name no BP money.

text: In 2022-23 Suncor Energy Foundation gave C$1M to C$4.99M, Shell Canada and RBC C$100k to C$250k; lifetime donors include Cenovus, BP Canada and Chevron Canada.
BP funding and information disclosure
A £50m, ten-year BP partnership was announced for the museum masterplan.
The museum said BP funding supports transformation and continued public access.

Emails released under freedom of information show BP, which paid for the museum's Days of the Dead festival with the Mexican Embassy, asking for confirmation of Mexican government representation, and of UK government representation through DCMS, at the private evening of 30 October 2015, as it prepared to bid for drilling licences in the Gulf of Mexico.

Emails in a Culture Unstained dossier show the museum's public affairs manager arranging a private meeting between Russia's ambassador, Alexander Yakovenko, two BP employees, director Hartwig Fischer and chair Richard Lambert on the morning of the Scythians press launch in May 2017, which the embassy called "very useful and positive".
The show coincided with new US Senate sanctions on Russia, where BP holds a large stake in Rosneft; the sources do not say what was discussed.

BP invited the Culture Secretary to its Annual Business Reception at the British Museum on 12 November 2015, and Baroness Neville-Rolfe, a minister at the business department, called in, according to freedom of information releases to the Art Not Oil Coalition.
A UK government hospitality return records BP giving Emily Walch, a special adviser at the business department, two tickets to a British Museum exhibition on 16 September 2014.

BP: £50M over ten years for the masterplan, announced 19 December 2023 (Museums Journal); the trustees put BP money and unspent income in a designated masterplan fund of £16.0M at 31 March 2026 (2025/26 accounts).
Trustee Ahdaf Soueif resigned over BP in 2019; 80 signed a 2023 open letter.
BP gives £50M over ten years for the masterplan, announced 19 December 2023.
BP Georgia is its standing corporate partner: on 20 October 2026 the homepage footer carries a BP logo linking to bpgeorgia.ge.

BP and its partners paid for the Rescue Archaeology Programme on the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan and South Caucasus pipelines in 2000 to 2005, and for the full cycle of survey, excavation, conservation, storage, exhibition and publication (BP volume, 2010).
It has a conservation laboratory at the Simon Janashia Museum and an auditorium, both set up with BP Georgia's support (BP volume, 2010).
BP is a current, long-running funder with a corporate-partner page on museum.ge.
In Norway's oil capital; no Equinor or Aker BP link found.

Région Hauts-de-France: 9 991 840 € statutory contribution in 2025, 8/10 under article 20 of the statutes, plus an exceptional 200 K€ subsidy voted on 27 November 2025; the region owns the building (budget report CFU 2025, BP 2026).
Département du Pas-de-Calais: 1 061 650 € in 2025, below the 1 248 980 € paid by the agglomeration for the same statutory tenth (budget report CFU 2025, BP 2026).
Communauté d'Agglomération Lens-Liévin: 1 248 980 € in 2025 (budget report CFU 2025, BP 2026).
State: 500 K€ a year for a new three-year period, 200 K€ more than before, plus 77 K€ in 2025 through the ANCT for work in priority neighbourhoods (budget report CFU 2025, BP 2026).
Ticketing: 1,08 M€ in 2025, close to 60% of it from temporary exhibitions; the Galerie du temps is free (budget report CFU 2025, BP 2026).

Patronage and space hire: 873 K€ in 2025, of which 540 K€ patronage: 277 K€ from members of the Cercle Louvre-Lens, 150 K€ from Crédit Mutuel for 'S'habiller en artiste' and 100 K€ from AXA for 'Gothiques' (budget report CFU 2025, BP 2026).
In-kind patronage: 137 K€ in 2025, of which 106 K€ from SFR for telephony and Wi-Fi over three years, and waste collection by Nicollin worth about 16 K€ (budget report CFU 2025, BP 2026).
Total expected revenue for 2026: 16 M€ (budget report CFU 2025, BP 2026).

The state pays 500 K€ a year under a three-year agreement, ticketing brought 1,08 M€ and patronage and space hire 873 K€ in 2025, with 150 K€ from Crédit Mutuel and 100 K€ from AXA for exhibitions (budget report CFU 2025, BP 2026).

Annual report 2024: main sponsors carried into 2025 are INPEX Idemitsu Petroleum Norge, Canica, Viking Cruises and Deloitte, with Bergesenstiftelsen, Sparebankstiftelsen DNB and Talent Norge as supporters; its thanks list also names Aker BP, Multiconsult and YARA.

The museum did not disclose sponsorship amounts: Kunstkritikk's request for the INPEX Idemitsu and Aker BP agreements was rejected in 2021, and the 2020 annual report showed own revenue covering about 19.6% of operating costs (Kunstkritikk, 2021).
BP: the galleries hosted the BP Portrait Award, shown in London first and then touring to Edinburgh; they ended it "in its present form" after the 2019 show (Hyperallergic, 11 November 2019).
Kept Baillie Gifford under protest; dropped BP 2019.

In February 2015 BP asked the gallery for at least 50 VIPs at the BP Portrait Award, with a breakdown that included government representatives, and in May a BP staff member proposed inviting Culture Minister Ed Vaizey to the award on 17 July, according to freedom of information releases to the Art Not Oil Coalition.

UK government hospitality returns record BP hosting Sue Owen, permanent secretary at the culture department, at the Portrait Award on 16 June 2015, and Sir Simon McDonald, head of the Foreign Office, at its Portrait Award reception on 11 June 2018.

Corporate partner: Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer, a supporter for about 20 years, now title sponsor of the Portrait Award in place of BP; Extinction Rebellion objected because its oil and gas team acts for BP and Chevron (The Art Newspaper, 15 November 2023).
The NPG exit followed those of Tate (2017), the Royal Shakespeare Company (2019) and the National Galleries of Scotland (2019) from BP (Hyperallergic).
The Gallery is one of those institutions; BP still sponsors the British Museum.
Refused Sackler £1M in 2019; BP award ended 2022.
A Cabinet Office hospitality return records its chief executive, John Manzoni, at the Royal Opera House on 10 June 2015 on tickets from Dev Sanyal of BP.

The Register of Members' Financial Interests records BP International giving the MP Robert Smith a ticket to the London 2012 gymnastics with meals at the BP Technology Showcase Exhibition at the Royal Opera House, value £750, on 30 July 2012.

The Register of Members' Financial Interests records BP International giving Jo Johnson, then a transport minister, and a guest hospitality at the Royal Opera House as part of BP's Big Screen programme, value £500, on 26 June 2018.
Ended BP in 2022 after 33 years.
BP exit is a partial sponsorship change
The museum group confirmed its BP partnership ended on 31 August 2026.
BP tie ended; Adani Green Energy remained associated with a gallery in the latest report.

BP's parliamentary submission describes its museum education collaboration and corporate learning objectives; a campaign investigation separately alleges decision powers in the historical research project.

Freedom of information releases to the Art Not Oil Coalition show BP's chief executive, Bob Dudley, inviting Culture Secretary John Whittingdale to the dinner the museum and BP gave for the opening of the Cosmonauts exhibition in 2015; he accepted and attended.

A month after the May 2015 election BP's government affairs staff met Culture Minister Ed Vaizey, who welcomed BP's support for Cosmonauts, and the rest of the meeting notes was withheld as relating to the development of government policy.
BP: sponsored the museum for nearly 25 years, including the former Energy Gallery, the 2015 Cosmonauts exhibition and the training academy; ended 31 August 2026 (The Art Newspaper).
A teachers' union urges schools to boycott the museum over Adani and BP sponsorship

The Art Newspaper reported on 10 June 2025 that the National Education Union backed a schools boycott of the Science Museum over its deals with BP and Adani Green Energy, a subsidiary of a group with weapons-manufacturing ties, with a union representative saying helping those companies "pull the wool over our eyes is not contributing to our children's education"; four London schools reportedly agreed not to send trips on the campaign's first day.

The Art Newspaper reported on 31 August 2026 that Chris Garrard of Culture Unstained said the museum had "finally come to its senses" when the BP deal ended, criticised the director for championing the partnership "year after year", and called it a "partial victory" because the Adani deal continues.
The BP sponsorship ended on 31 August 2026 after about 25 years.
Adani Green since 2024; BP ended only in August 2026.
Ended BP in 2016 after protests; Sackler name removed 2022.
Proposal pitched to BP Canada March 2025.
The Guardian's 2015 petition and the 2022 sale of BP and Shell shares concern the Trust's investments, not the museum.
Wellcome faced a divestment call in March 2015 over fossil-fuel holdings and sold its BP and Shell shares in 2022.

36th Bienal sponsors: strategic partner Itaú; master sponsors Bloomberg, Bradesco, Petrobras, Instituto Cultural Vale, Citi Brasil and Vivo; also Motiva, Open Society Foundations, Alupar, Iguatemi and Rolex; Royal Air Maroc as carrier (Times Brasil, September 2025).
Itaú and Bradesco are also sponsors (Carta Capital).
Nubank (R$10M a year to 2027, about 40% of budget), Bradesco and others. 98% of funds come through the Rouanet tax law; free entry.

Private sector at 31 December 2024: Vale R$ 50,5 milhões; Bradesco R$ 50 milhões; Itaú R$ 10 milhões; Eletrobras R$ 5 milhões; Cosan R$ 3,1 milhões.
Sponsor ranks now: platinum Vale and Bradesco; silver Itaú; bronze Axia Energia and Cosan; support from J.P.

Master sponsors Bradesco, InfinitePay, Itaú, Vivo, Chanel.

Eli Broad was founding chairman (Wikipedia).

Eli Broad's fortune came from insurance and home construction (The Art Newspaper).
Founded by Eli and Edythe Broad.

Barrikaden, Camps, Sekundenkleber"; Porsche Holding Salzburg for the start of a multi-year partnership and free-entry days (also a TikTok video for the free-entry day, "sponsored by Porsche Holding Salzburg"); CC Real GmbH for "PECHE POP" and advertising space at Wien Mitte The Mall; Wiener Städtische for free entry on MAK Day; Flughafen Wien AG for advertising screens; Swarovski for a floral installation; Ernst Ploil for the "PECHE POP" catalogue; Dorotheum for "ICONIC AUBÖCK"; Vöslauer and Ottakringer as event partners.

What is there: more than 80,000 works from 100 A.D. to the present (Google Arts & Culture), 79,000 in The Canadian Encyclopedia: European painting by Rembrandt, Hals, Poussin, Chardin and Picasso, Canadian art from the 18th century on, Inuit, African and Oceanic art, photography, and the Henry Moore Sculpture Centre, the largest public collection of Moore's work outside the UK; Kenneth Thomson gave over 2,000 works, and every work was donated or bought with income from donations (The Canadian Encyclopedia; The Art Newspaper, 9 November 2026).

Photographs are also online through Brasiliana Fotográfica, made with the Fundação Biblioteca Nacional, and Google Arts & Culture since 2012 (institute website).

A museum of Fernando Botero's gift to Colombia in a colonial house in La Candelaria, Bogotá, which was the archbishop's office until 1955 and which Banco de la República restored and adapted under Botero's guidance (Google Arts & Culture partner page).

Botero (1932 to 2023) gave the collection to Banco de la República, Colombia's central bank, in 2000, and the museum has been open free of charge since 1 November 2000 (Banco de la República, 15 September 2023; Google Arts & Culture partner page).

The oldest is Camille Corot's Gitane au tambourin, from before 1862, and the newest a 1998 oil by Barceló; other artists are Picasso, Léger, Renoir, Monet, Dalí, Miró, Giacometti, Beckmann, Freud, Calder and Bacon (Google Arts & Culture partner page; Banco de la República, 15 September 2023).

Contemporary art museum in Dolapdere, Beyoğlu, a working-class Istanbul neighbourhood (Qantara), run as a non-profit by the Vehbi Koç Foundation (VKV).

The collection, started in 2007, holds more than 1,300 works, about half by Turkish artists. Ömer Koç, a third-generation Koç and collector, chairs Arter, and Melih Fereli is director (The Art Newspaper).

In 2013 protests targeted 13th Istanbul Biennial events over sponsor Koç Holding; at a 10 May action activists wore Koç banners and the names of gentrifying neighbourhoods, and over 100 people in the Turkish art world issued a statement criticising the curators' response (ArtInfo, republished by ArtLeaks).

Koç Holding's 2024 revenue was $65.8 billion.

Its refiner Tüpraş runs most of Turkey's oil refineries and makes up almost half the group's revenue; its subsidiary Otokar is a bus and military vehicle maker (Wikipedia, Koç Holding and Otokar pages).

Whether the foundation holds Koç assets is unknown.

Director Hong Ra-hee resigns a second time amid a Samsung scandal

The Korea Times reported on 6 March 2017 that Hong Ra-hee resigned as director of Leeum and of the Ho-Am Art Museum, and that insiders linked this to the arrest in February of her son, Samsung Electronics vice chairman Lee Jae-yong, on bribery and other charges.

ArtAsiaPacific reported the same day that it was her second resignation over a Samsung scandal: in 2008 her husband Lee Kun-hee was charged with tax evasion and reports described a slush fund of over USD 60 million allegedly used to buy more than 30 artworks, and she returned in March 2011.
Director Hong Ra-hee resigned in 2008 during a Samsung slush fund investigation, returned in 2011 and resigned again in March 2017 after her son's indictment.
